_doc: *** PROPOSAL DRAFT — NOT CANON, NOT RATIFIED, NOT WIRED TO ANYTHING ***
The HANGING-VALLEY / WATER-GAP geography, built so it can be judged instead of
argued about. Deliberately NOT placed in public/world/ and NOT read by
worldmap_validate, valley_map, valley_build or any shipped scene: this file
exists only to drive tools/owdraft_{lib,layout,build,render,export}.py.
THE PROPOSITION, in one sentence: Emberbrook sits in a HANGING VALLEY cradled
behind an unbroken mountain arm; the range breaks at exactly ONE notch where
the river leaves; beyond that notch the land FALLS, and the falling reach is
the Emberbrook->Dellhollow road, maturing into Dellhollow's lock-gorge.
FRAME: [x, y] = east, north, over [0,300] x [0,240], miniature world units
(character = 1.45u), same unit convention as public/world/world.json. This is a
BIGGER tile than the shipped 280x200 valley because the corridor is the subject
here, not a stretch of it.
ORIENTATION NOTE (this is the whole argument, stated up front): the draft takes
its orientation from the TOWN maps, which both say downstream = NORTH -- the
Emberbrook map's river flows south->north past the Old Gate 'toward Dellhollow
beyond', and Dellhollow's own frame declares 'x = along-gorge (downstream/north
positive)'. The ratified public/world/world.json says downstream = SOUTH-EAST.
They cannot both be true. See the report's conflict list.
name: The Ember Corridor (draft)

farField._doc: what the land does once it is out of the corridor's reach: a gentle continued climb (a dead-flat far field shows as radiating facets in any hillshade) plus the Whisperwood's own hill country, so the drafted valley reads as ONE valley among implied others.

_doc: ONE river, source to Ch3 exit. Per point: [x, y, waterHeight, width, clear,
rise, riseDist] where clear = bank height above water, rise = further climb
from bank to shoulder, riseDist = the horizontal run that climb takes.
The hanging valley reach is WIDE and GENTLE (clear ~1.2, rise over 55u); the
gorge reach is NARROW and TALL (clear 3->16, rise over 16-24u).
Monotonically descending, and the descent is the point.

_doc: Whisperwood road (SOUTH, upstream) -> Emberbrook -> the Old Gate at the notch
-> down the gorge's RIGHT bank (east side, facing downstream) -> the bench ->
Dellhollow's rim Valley Gate. The road NEVER crosses the water.
ABOVE THE GATE the course is authored on gentle ground; the z is the map's.
BELOW THE GATE 'bench' gives [s, offset, h]: arc-length along the river, how
far to its RIGHT the ledge sits, and the ledge's height.  MEASURED FIRST:
the natural gorge profile offers NO bench at those offsets — a V has none, the
land there stands 20-23u above the water — so the ledge is CARVED (shelf,
below), which is what the shipped valley.region.json also does (canyon.shelf,
width 6.0, backRise 22.0).  Reported rather than hidden: this geography does
not hand you a road, you cut one.
The zig-zag in the offsets IS the switchback flight below the falls.

shelf._doc: the ledge: flat to halfWidth, then back UP into the wall over backRun on the hill side, and OFF the edge over outerRun on the river side. Wall above, drop below, the wall always on the traveller's right.

_doc: The renders the brief asks for. pos/target in the draft world frame [x, y, h];
snapToGround puts the eye at ground + 1.5u, plus any 'lift'. Every sight line
is marched against the field by tools/owdraft_cams.py BEFORE rendering — 'in
frame' is not 'visible' (DAYLOG). Two of the three MOVED because this geography
occludes itself, and that is the finding, not a camera problem:
* the aerial cannot see the corridor from the south at ANY height — the
unbroken range hides its own gorge. It works only looking straight DOWN
the corridor axis, through the gap.
* from the Old Gate you see 52u down the gorge and no further; Dellhollow is
90u on, round two bends. The eye also needs ~9u of lift to see past the
cleft's own walls, so 'fromgate' is a drone height, not a walker's.
* from Dellhollow NOTHING of the notch, the falls or the upper gorge is
visible from any standable point (the notch would need an eye 55.5u up).

aerial.note: (a) the whole corridor, along its axis and through the gap

fromgate.note: (b) at the Old Gate, looking down the gorge. Dellhollow is NOT in it.

fromdell.note: (c) from Dellhollow, up the gorge. The range and the notch are NOT in it, and cannot be.

gatehero.note: supporting frame: the Old Gate in its notch from the valley side, road over and water under
